subject: Interim: streaming pacing delay affecting partial responses (CobaltHealth)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Smith <avery.smith@cobalthealth.com>, eng-ops@cobalthealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Interim: streaming pacing delay affecting partial responses (CobaltHealth)

Hi Avery / Cobalt ops team,

I'm writing to let you know we've observed a degradation impacting streaming responses for a subset of request traffic to your account starting ~08:45 PST. Symptoms: some generation streams end prematurely (client sees a finalization event with fewer tokens than expected) or display pauses between chunks for 0.5–2s for ~7% of requests.

What we've done so far:
- Activated warm-pool routing for CobaltHealth requests at 08:55 PST to reduce cold-kv latency.
- Temporarily increased per-model concurrency for your tenant to reduce request queuing.
- Enabled a retry-safety header on the gateway for affected endpoints to prevent duplicate side effects.

Immediate impact: user-facing partial streams and elongated chunk gaps. We estimate ~7% of generation calls during the window experienced visible degradation. No data exfiltration or unauthorized access detected.

Next steps (short):
- We're running a focused investigation to determine root cause; initial signal points to a pacing interaction between continuous batching and a new prefetch path.
- Will provide a targeted timeline and an operational mitigation by 12:30 PST.
- We'll share a post-incident timeline and a follow-up postmortem once we confirm root cause.

Please let me know if this is causing urgent user-facing outages for you (e.g., automated pipelines that must be paused). We're prioritizing CobaltHealth on this.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep this thread updated.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-12T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interim: streaming pacing delay affecting partial responses (CobaltHealth)

Rishi — noted. Brief update from infra/serving: we've rolled a hotfix candidate to the canary pool that adjusts the prefetch pacing window (commit 9f4b3a) and observed a drop from 7% -> ~2% in canary traffic. Ops will continue ramping if stability holds.

Action items: 
- Hannah, please coordinate with Platform to keep Cobalt routed to the warm pool and block automated scaling changes until we validate metrics for 30m.
- Ben, please prepare a short customer-facing timeline and include a short FAQ for Cobalt's SREs about recommended retry/backoff behavior.
- Rishi, if Cobalt asks for an interim SLA credit, run it by me before committing.

I'll update in 30 minutes with canary results.

Thanks —
Marissa
Head of Incident Response, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Interim: streaming pacing delay affecting partial responses (CobaltHealth)

Please keep us posted on ETA for full remediation; if you have a recommended temporary retry/timeout config for our side that reduces duplicate work we'd appreciate it.

Also, heads up: we have an internal compliance sync at 11:00 PST — if you have any customer-facing text we can share with stakeholders that would help, please send.

— Avery
Director, Platform Engineering, CobaltHealth
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Smith <avery.smith@cobalthealth.com>, eng-ops@cobalthealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-12T15:48:00-08:00
Subject: Post-impact update and next steps — streaming pacing event (CobaltHealth)

Hi Avery / team,

Quick update following our mitigation and root-cause triage:
- Mitigation timeline: hotfix rolled to production at 10:20 PST (commit 9f4b3a), warm-pool routing kept active until 14:15 PST. Observed error surface return to baseline (<=0.5% affected) by ~11:10 PST and sustained through the afternoon.
- Root cause (interim): an interaction between the new prefetch path and continuous-batcher pacing algorithm caused intermittent underdrain of the KV prefetch buffer. In short: some requests entered the batch without ready KV state which produced elongated chunk gaps and early stream finalization.
- Impact: estimated 7% of streaming requests for your tenant between 08:45–11:10 PST experienced partial or paused streams. No customer data leakage.

Attached: investigation-log-20261212.txt (traces and relevant spans), timeline-20261212.csv (event timeline), and a customer communication draft you can share with stakeholders. Full postmortem doc is being prepared and will land in 48–72 hours with a permanent remediation plan (changes to prefetch safety checks and additional canary gating).

Temporary guidance for CobaltHealth engineers (to reduce duplicate processing while we finalize fixes):
- Prefer idempotent ingestion: include request_id and dedupe downstream by request_id.
- Increase stream receive timeout to 10s and enable client-side tolerant re-assembly (we can share example code).
- If you must retry, use exponential backoff with jitter starting at 300ms.

If you'd like a 30-minute technical sync in the next 24 hours to walk through traces and remediation, I can schedule time with the on-call engineers.

Apologies again for the disruption. We'll follow up with a full RCA and planned mitigations.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
